That's the messy-input guard settled. A few remaining "what if" situations to close out — two I can just confirm the intended behavior with you in words (they're about a rule or can't be reliably staged in a prototype), and one you can see directly.

**A) See it: long titles and lots of links.** In the current prototype (**http://maker:4001**), please paste a very long address (say a long article URL) and add several tags. Confirm the card **wraps neatly** — long titles/addresses don't overflow, and many tags flow onto multiple lines — and that adding a bunch of links just scrolls normally. Does the layout hold up for you?

**B) Confirm the rule: when the page title can't be read.** Sometimes a page won't give up its title (it's down, or blocks it). My intended behavior: **still save the link**, and simply **show the web address as the title** (which you can rename anytime with the pencil) — rather than refusing to save or leaving it blank. Does that match what you'd want?

**C) Confirm the rule: your links are still there when you come back.** This is central to it being a *dependable* place. My intent: everything you save — links, tags, read-later flags, archive — **persists**, so when you close the browser and return later, it's all exactly as you left it. Is that the expectation? (And since you said this is just for you: is it fine that it's *your* personal collection on your own device, with no login/accounts in this first version?)
